blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
People analytics has matured from novelty into a legitimate discipline. A decade ago, HR functions produced descriptive dashboards — how many employees, how many leavers, how many hires. Today, leading teams run predictive models, conduct controlled experiments and partner with data scientists to test causal hypotheses.

With that maturity comes greater responsibility. Correlation is not causation, and even the most elegant model can mislead if the underlying data is biased or incomplete. A good people analyst is, above all, intellectually honest: willing to say "the evidence suggests, but does not prove", rather than dressing up opinion in the language of science.

The strategic value lies in the questions, not the tools. The right question — "Which managers retain talent significantly above the organisational average, and what do they actually do differently?" — often produces more insight than a twenty-tab dashboard that answers none of the questions that leaders truly care about.

items.q: According to the text, what did HR functions mainly produce a decade ago?
items.why: "HR functions produced descriptive dashboards — how many employees, how many leavers, how many hires."

items.q: What does the author say an elegant model can still do?
options: Mislead if the underlying data is biased or incomplete
items.why: "even the most elegant model can mislead if the underlying data is biased or incomplete."

items.q: The author suggests that the strategic value of people analytics lies mainly in…
options: the number of tabs in the dashboard
the size of the data science team
items.why: "The strategic value lies in the questions, not the tools."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Correlation and causation are not the same thing.
Biased data can undermine even a sophisticated model.
Analysts should admit when evidence is only suggestive.
A twenty-tab dashboard is more valuable than one well-framed question.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que uma boa pergunta rende mais que um dashboard de vinte abas.

items.q: The phrase "dressing up opinion in the language of science" suggests that the author disapproves of analysts who…
options: make opinions sound like proven facts
admit the limits of their data
items.why: Inferência: 'dressing up opinion' = disfarçar opinião de ciência, algo que o autor critica em favor da honestidade intelectual.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry comentando o estudo de engajamento com a equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, I've read the study three times now, and I want us to be careful before we take that eighteen percent to the board. The headline is seductive — a new engagement programme, productivity up eighteen percent — but the more I look at it, the more cautious I become.

Here's my worry. The teams that opted into the programme were, on average, already the higher performers. That's a classic confounding variable. So the number may reflect who joined, not what the programme actually did. The evidence suggests an effect, but it certainly doesn't prove one.

And the sample is small — barely forty people across two sites. With numbers that thin, I'd hesitate to claim anything with confidence. I'm not saying the programme failed; I'm saying we don't yet know.

What I'd propose is a proper controlled comparison next quarter — randomise who takes part, hold the conditions steady, and then measure. If the effect survives that, I'll be the first to champion it upstairs. Until then, let's report it as promising but unproven, and resist the temptation to overclaim.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Harry cautious about the eighteen percent figure?
options: The data scientists disagreed with him
The teams that joined were already higher performers
The board asked him to lower the number
items.why: "the teams that opted into the programme were, on average, already the higher performers."

items.q: What technical problem does Harry identify with the study?
items.why: "That's a classic confounding variable."

items.q: What does Harry say about the sample?
options: It is small — barely forty people across two sites
items.why: "the sample is small — barely forty people across two sites."

items.q: What can we infer about Harry's overall position on the programme?
options: He is genuinely undecided and wants better evidence
items.why: Inferência: 'I'm not saying the programme failed; I'm saying we don't yet know' — ele suspende o juízo à espera de evidência.

items.q: What does Harry's proposal for next quarter reveal about how he thinks?
options: He wants to avoid measuring anything
He values a controlled test over a headline number
items.why: Inferência: propor randomização e condições controladas mostra preferência por inferência causal, não por manchete.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The uplift may be driven by a confounding variable we haven't measured." A confounding variable is…
options: a variable with no effect at all
a hidden factor that distorts the apparent relationship
items.why: Variável de confusão: um fator oculto que influencia o resultado e distorce a relação observada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "With such a small ___, the confidence interval is far too wide to draw firm conclusions."
items.why: Sample size = tamanho da amostra; amostra pequena gera intervalos de confiança amplos.

items.q: "We found a strong correlation between training hours and retention." A correlation tells you that…
options: one variable definitely causes the other
two variables move together, without proving cause
items.why: Correlação = associação estatística entre variáveis; não implica causalidade.

items.q: An actionable insight is best described as…
options: a raw export of the database
a finding leaders can actually act on
items.why: Insight acionável: uma conclusão que orienta uma decisão ou ação concreta.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Before we run the numbers, let's state the ___ we're actually testing."
items.why: Hypothesis = hipótese: a afirmação que o estudo se propõe a testar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem ao discutir estudos e dados. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I don't want us to overclaim on the strength of one small study." To overclaim means to…
options: state more than the evidence supports
items.why: Overclaim = afirmar excessivamente, ir além do que os dados sustentam.

items.q: "Let's drill down into the manager-level data before we generalise." To drill down into means to…
items.why: Drill down into = descer ao detalhe, analisar em granularidade mais fina.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the causal claim." They…
items.why: Push back on = contestar, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "On closer reading, the correlation doesn't hold up." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = resistir ao escrutínio, continuar válido quando examinado de perto.

items.q: "A tidier dashboard won't move the needle on decision quality." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, gerar diferença perceptível.
